about: Long-term value investing in large, durable businesses.

holdings.name: New York Times Company
holdings.filedName: NEW YORK TIMES CO MTN BE

summary: Concentrated: 29 holdings, but the top ten are 88% of the portfolio.
Trades moderately: about 22% of the portfolio changes in a year.
The average holding, by value, has been owned for at least 8.3 years.
Compared with the typical S&P 500 company, its holdings are similarly priced, more profitable and much larger.
Copying each filing beat the S&P 500 in 3 of 9 full years.

profile.background: Took control of Berkshire Hathaway, then a struggling textile company, in 1965 and turned it into a holding company that owns businesses outright and large stakes in listed companies. He stepped down as chief executive at the end of 2025 and remains chairman; Greg Abel, who has run Berkshire's non-insurance businesses since 2018, became chief executive in 2026.
profile.approach: Buys large, durable businesses with lasting competitive advantages and able management, at sensible prices, and holds them for many years.
known: Berkshire's share price compounded at 19.9% a year from 1965 to 2024, against 10.4% for the S&P 500 with dividends (Berkshire's 2024 shareholder letter, as reported).
The 13F covers only Berkshire's US-listed shares, not the companies it owns outright or its cash.
profile.note: From 2026 these decisions are Berkshire's under Greg Abel, not Buffett's alone.

sources.title: Buffett to retire as CEO at the end of 2025 (KTVU/AP)
